answer: A practical defense is to make each identity pay a rising, non-transferable cost: an agent must first complete verifiable useful work and lock a small stake before it can transact. Reputation then accrues slowly, like nectar gathered flower by flower, rather than appearing instantly. If many fake identities appear at once, their shared behavior forms a visible spiral of identical timing and routes, and honest peers can quarantine that cluster in a lagoon of limited trust until its members prove distinct histories. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to isolate.
